candidates.name: BOEING 2707
candidates.caption: America wanted its own supersonic future. The prototype never reached the runway.
candidates.why_unbuilt: US government funding ended in 1971 before the flight prototype was completed.
candidates.what_remains: Mock-up sections and engineering records preserve the proposed supersonic airliner.
candidates.note: *1966 marks selection of Boeing for the US SST prototype programme, not the start of all design work. The 2707 changed configuration; distinguish the early swing-wing and later fixed-wing versions when creating artwork.

candidates.name: TATLIN'S TOWER
candidates.caption: A revolution imagined in iron and glass. Its headquarters remained a model.
candidates.why_unbuilt: The monumental design remained unrealised; its precise construction barriers need further source review.
candidates.what_remains: Drawings, photographs, and reconstructed models preserve its intertwined spirals and suspended volumes.
candidates.note: Monument to the Third International. The museum confirms the full structure was never built and describes its 1979 reconstruction. Do not present the reconstructed model as the original. Verify cost/material explanations before promotion.

candidates.name: PROJECT DAEDALUS
candidates.caption: A starship designed to cross the distance. Its first journey was through an engineering report.
candidates.why_unbuilt: Daedalus was a volunteer feasibility study, not a funded spacecraft construction programme.
candidates.what_remains: The 1978 report and later interstellar studies retain its two-stage fusion-probe concept.
candidates.note: The BIS describes a 1973–1978 volunteer study targeting a flyby of Barnard’s Star. The study was completed, not cancelled; do not confuse an unbuilt vehicle with a failed research programme.
